question: Can generated TypeScript avoid context-sensitive name-loop prediction in routine_name and general_element without changing Oracle parse behavior?
hypothesis: The routine_name dotted-name loop can resolve clean input with two-token lookahead, and both general_element dotted-part loops can skip prediction when PERIOD cannot follow, while every accepted construct, diagnostic, and parse tree remains unchanged.
conformanceCommand: LAB_TREE_HASH=1 node grammar/typescript/harness.ts with LAB_GENERATED_OPTIMIZATIONS=generalElementPart for the control and generalElement,generalElementPart,routineName for the candidate
independentTailCommand: Generate each optimization state separately, then run node scripts/benchmarkProduction.ts .work/private-production/tail-manifest.json 3 <opaque-result-name>
selection: Complete frozen 1,244-file opaque production corpus; tail statistics reuse the 12 opaque ids selected by experiment 004.
candidate: Post-process the generated TypeScript routine_name loop with PERIOD plus id_expression lookahead on clean input, and gate both general_element dotted-part loop predictions with the PERIOD FIRST token.
acceptance: The 12-file tail has a repeatable parser-core reduction against the post-#1 control.
The complete corpus has zero per-file differences in parse-tree digest, lexer and parser diagnostics, visible and hidden tokens, prediction mode, and SLL/LL attempts.
The candidate retains adaptive prediction where caller context can make a period belong outside the loop.
Only opaque file identities, hashes, and aggregate evidence leave the private corpus.
limitations: The tail selection is inherited from experiment 004 and is intentionally biased to the highest-cost files.
Three repetitions give a descriptive deterministic bootstrap interval, not a production guarantee.
Java remains an unmodified control and does not include the TypeScript generated-code optimization.
The laboratory has no production semantic indexer; identical parse trees are the semantic-consumer boundary.
Generated-shape checks fail loudly, but the transforms remain coupled to pinned antlr-ng output rather than to generator-level FIRST-set APIs.
